pr_title: Bluetooth: MPL: Modify parse_search to use bt_data_parse
pr_body:
Modify the implementation of parse_search to use a net_buf_simple and bt_data_parse to parse the LTV
search structure.

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/58554
pr_comments: It seems to me that the parsing is not completely equivalent. It's no longer testing the type field of the ADs. It's not explained in the commit message. Is this correct?

> It seems to me that the parsing is not completely equivalent. It's no longer testing the type field of the ADs. It's not explained in the commit message. Is this correct?

Ah, thanks for catching that. Yes, this is no longer returning an error on invalid type. I'll go ahead and fix that :)

review_comments: While this might work right now, I don't think the `bt_data_parse()` API gives any promises of `buf.len != 0U` being a reliable way of determining whether parsing was successful or not. A more reliable way would be e.g. to pass `&search_failed` as user data to the callback.

I agree, but I think we will find a lot more errors in the LE Audio stack if that changes :) Suggest to revisit this issue once we have a better way of handling const data where this will be refactored anyhow
It would be nice to have a `struct net_buf_simple_ro` for cases like this. Should we open an issue on this?

@alwa-nordic Yes, I agree. We would really appreciate something like that for LE audio where we have a lot of `const` data. I even implemented a temporary solution

```c
int bt_audio_data_parse(const uint8_t ltv[], size_t size,
			bool (*func)(struct bt_data *data, void *user_data), void *user_data);
```

for one of my PRs (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/58331) until a simple buf works with `const` data. 

I was planning on make such a feature request once I figured out whether it should be a read-only `net_buf_simple` or perhaps if the new struct should be a `net_buf_simple_mut`, as I somewhat expect the majority of cases for `net_buf_simple` is to read data rather that to modify it.
